title: Completed differentials over a field as ordinary differentials over pth-power parameters
statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $r\geq0$, and $B=F[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $(C,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local $F$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $u:B\to C$ be a continuous local $F$-algebra homomorphism for the $(T_1,\ldots,T_r)$-adic and $\mathfrak m$-adic topologies. Assume $C$ is a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Put $B_1=F[[T_1^p,\ldots,T_r^p]]\subseteq B$, the subring of series whose exponents are divisible by $p$ in every coordinate, with its induced map to $C$. For Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], put $\widehat\Omega_{C/F}=\varprojlim_n\Omega_{C/F}/\mathfrak m^n\Omega_{C/F}$. The canonical $F$-derivation $C\to\widehat\Omega_{C/F}$ vanishes on $u(B_1)$, and its induced $C$-linear map $\Omega_{C/B_1}\to\widehat\Omega_{C/F}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: EGA 0_IV Lemma 21.9.4, printed p.177 (PDF p.177), with the stronger module-finite hypothesis in place of finite type over B; proof uses 20.7.14.4 and 20.4.7. Also ILO IV 2.1.6, printed p.51, the identification before equation (2.b).

proof.text: Because $C$ is finite over $B=F[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]$, its residue field $C/\mathfrak m$ is a finite-dimensional $F$-algebra and, since $C$ is local, a finite field extension of the image of $F$. Thus the hypotheses of [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal] apply with $A=C$ and $M_F(C)=\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$. We obtain that $\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ is a finite $C$-module, is generated by the elements $d_Fc$, and represents $F$-derivations from $C$ to every finite $\mathfrak m$-adically complete $C$-module.

source.place: 0_IV 21.9.1 and 21.9.4; the finiteness of the residue field extension follows from the finite B-module hypothesis

proof.text: The ring $B_1=F[[T_1^p,\ldots,T_r^p]]$ is a formal power series ring over $F$, and $B$ is finite free over $B_1$ with basis the monomials $T_1^{a_1}\cdots T_r^{a_r}$ for $0\leq a_i<p$. Hence $C$ is finite over $B_1$. By the universal presentation of Kähler differentials, $\Omega_{C/B_1}$ is generated by the differentials of a finite set of $B_1$-algebra generators of $C$, so it is a finite $C$-module. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] with $R=C$, $J=\mathfrak m$ shows that $\Omega_{C/B_1}$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete.

source.place: 0_IV 21.9.4, first paragraph; finite monomial decomposition over the pth-power parameter ring

proof.text: Let $d_F:C\to\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ be the canonical derivation, the composite of $C\to\Omega_{C/F}$ with the map to the inverse limit. Its restriction to the image of the polynomial subring $F[T_1^p,\ldots,T_r^p]$ is zero: it kills $F$, and $d_F(u(T_i)^p)=p\,u(T_i)^{p-1}d_Fu(T_i)=0$ in characteristic $p$. Let $b\in B_1$ and $N\geq1$. Truncating its expansion, $b=g+h$ with $g\in F[T_1^p,\ldots,T_r^p]$ and $h\in(T_1,\ldots,T_r)^{N}B$; since $u$ is local, $u(T_i)\in\mathfrak m$, so $u(h)\in\mathfrak m^N$. By the Leibniz rule $d_F(\mathfrak m^N)\subseteq\mathfrak m^{N-1}\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$, hence $d_F(u(b))=d_F(u(h))\in\mathfrak m^{N-1}\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ for every $N$. The module $\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically separated: $\mathfrak m^k\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ maps to zero in $\Omega_{C/F}/\mathfrak m^k\Omega_{C/F}$, so $\bigcap_k\mathfrak m^k\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ lies in the kernel of every projection of the inverse limit, which is zero. Therefore $d_F$ vanishes on $u(B_1)$ and is a $B_1$-derivation. The universal property of Kähler differentials then gives a canonical $C$-linear map $\alpha:\Omega_{C/B_1}\to\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ with $\alpha(d_{B_1}c)=d_Fc$.

source.place: 0_IV 21.9.4, proof: derivations vanish on the dense polynomial subring and hence on B^p

proof.text: The universal derivation $d_{B_1}:C\to\Omega_{C/B_1}$ is also an $F$-derivation. Its target is finite and complete by Step 2, so the universal property in [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal] gives a unique $C$-linear map $\beta:\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}\to\Omega_{C/B_1}$ satisfying $\beta(d_Fc)=d_{B_1}c$ for every $c\in C$.

source.place: 0_IV 21.9.4, use of the completed universal property

proof.text: For every $c\in C$, $(\beta\circ\alpha)(d_{B_1}c)=d_{B_1}c$ and $(\alpha\circ\beta)(d_Fc)=d_Fc$. The elements $d_{B_1}c$ generate $\Omega_{C/B_1}$ by its defining construction, while the elements $d_Fc$ generate $\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$ by Step 1. Hence $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are inverse isomorphisms. The first map is exactly the canonical map induced by the continuous $F$-derivation $C\to\widehat{\Omega}_{C/F}$, proving the claim.

proof_origin.place: EGA 0_IV Lemma 21.9.4, printed p.177 (PDF p.177), proof by density of the pth-power polynomial subring and the completed universal property (20.7.14.4).
